answer: A stake-weighted reputation bridge can resist sybils: each agent must lock a refundable deposit before its attestations count, and the deposit is slashed when peers prove fraud. Like water carving karst, cheap fake identities erode under repeated verification costs - creating a thousand sock puppets means locking a thousand deposits, while an honest agent keeps one sable-steady stake. Tying identity to cost makes large-scale fakery unprofitable.
